comment: The filing path's one-value-per-namespace refusal (`fix-issue-filing-state-namespace`, issue #179), the two required fields that are labels (issue #201), and the answer shape's one home (issue #859). At filing time there is nothing to displace, so a merged label set naming two values of one namespace is a refusal, not the replacement `update.sh` performs for the state namespace; and because `create.sh` insists on a finding's `class` and `category`, both join the label set — the mutation that removes the join must be visible in the case that asserts it. 2.1 and 2.2 are the shape's home: #845 declared it in `tools/issues/lib.sh` and left the filing path spelling both halves out, so each constant is mutated in the library and the case that reads the recorded answer must go red — on the base both mutations stayed green, because the two literals in `create.sh` were independent of the constants. Run it with `bash tools/mutate.sh --mutations tools/issues/tests/create-mutations.json`; `.pi/skills/mutation-runner` owns how, `.pi/skills/revert-check` owns the rule, and the CI step that owns the issue tooling prints `--list`, so a set that no longer parses fails the pipeline instead of rotting. The search is a single line and unique in its file (the runner's replacement is literal and line-based).

mutations.why: a filing whose merged label set names two values of one namespace being refused before any gh issue create
the filing path refusing a citation that repeats its own directory, so the item is not born stale (#189)
the finding's required class and category reaching the tracker as labels (issue #201), so a finding that names its kind only in the two fields cannot file an item no selector reads
the answer's first half having one home (issue #859) — the filing path writes the decision line from this constant, so moving it moves the recorded answer
the same home for the marker half (issue #859) — the filing path binds each decision to its question with this constant, so moving it moves the comment it writes
